companionPayload.note: RECONCILED 2026-09-07 (CTX-B dispatch, operator-ruled) between this repo's prior 4-district Article-II-single-family-only table and legacy-design-tools' independently-researched 10-district table, both derived from City of Round Rock Zoning and Development Code, Code of Ordinances Part III (2018 Edition), Chapter 2, Article II (Residential Districts), Section 2-26 (Residential Lot and Building Dimensional Standards), retrieved via https://roundrock-tx.elaws.us/code/coor_ptiii_ch2_artii_sec2-26 (Round Rock's own library.municode.com pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetch; no field here reaches human-verified against a real code-section atom -- round_rock_tx has 361 real atoms and Sections 1-50/2-26 both exist as real ingested atoms, but neither atom's bodyText captures the dimensional-standards chart's actual cell values, a table-extraction gap, not a corpus absence -- so every field here is primary-source-verified). RULING 1 (side_corner_ft, ALL 10 districts): this repo's DERIVATION wins over the other table's assumption. Chapter 1 definitions, Section 1-50 ('Front Lot Line'), state 'In cases where two or more lot lines abut an existing or dedicated street, all such lot lines are considered front lot lines for the purposes of calculating building setbacks' -- a general Chapter 1 rule, not limited to Article II's single-family rows -- so side_corner_ft = front_ft on every district Article II tabulates no separate corner figure for. The other table instead mirrored the base side setback (an unmotivated assumption, and the permissive/smaller-setback direction for a buildable envelope) on all 10 districts; that reasoning is superseded here. One district, TH (Townhouse, Single-lot), is the exception: Section 2-26's own row tabulates an explicit adjacent-to-street side value ('5 ft./20 ft.' interior/adjacent-to-street) rather than leaving a blank cell for Section 1-50 to fill, so TH's side_corner_ft is that directly-tabulated 20 ft, not a Section-1-50 derivation off its 15 ft front_ft (the other table's own provenance quote already named this 20 ft value but the table's stored side_corner_ft field left it at 5, mirroring side_ft instead -- a bug, corrected here, not a re-derivation). RULING 1 AMENDMENT (2026-09-07, second review): MF-2 was flagged, then resolved. Applying the derivation there would produce 15 ft, LOOSER than the superseded side-mirror convention's 25 ft (MF-2 is the only district where front_ft < side_ft, so the derivation loosens instead of tightens). A derivation is trustworthy when it tightens a figure (safe if the underlying legal reasoning turns out imprecise) and is NOT sufficient on its own when it loosens one (unsafe if wrong) -- so MF-2's side_corner_ft is REFUSED rather than derived: no primary-source citation was found for a distinct MF-2 corner value, and 25 ft (the more conservative candidate) is carried as a not_specified placeholder pending one. Every other district's derivation was checked against this same tighten/loosen test and tightens (or, for SR, is unchanged): none of the other 9 needed this exception. RULING 2 (district breadth): all 10 districts (SF-R, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, MH, TF, TH, SR, MF-1, MF-2) are carried, not just the 4 this file previously shipped -- six districts do not fall to absence. RULING 3 (SF-3 side_ft/rear_ft): REFUSED, not picked. The two source tables read different, genuinely different sub-columns of the same Section 2-26 SF-3 chart cell -- this file's prior research read the zero-lot-line option (side_ft=12, rear_ft=15), the other table read the Standard-Lot sub-column (side_ft=5, rear_ft=10) -- and a parcel's GIS zoningCode of 'SF-3' cannot distinguish which sub-type actually applies on the ground. Both are defensible, differently-reasoned readings of the same table cell, not an error on either side. side_ft and rear_ft below carry the zero-lot-line reading (12/15, the larger, more conservative pair) ONLY as a required-by-schema numeric placeholder, flagged not_specified: true with an explicit refusal quote -- a correct reader must treat SF-3's side_ft/rear_ft as unresolved pending a real per-parcel sub-type read, not as a settled value. RULING 4 (max_height_ft sentinel): unified to 999 (this file's prior value) across all districts, not 100 (the other table's prior value) -- both were flagged not_specified: true, but 999 cannot be mistaken for a real building height in feet the way 100 (a physically plausible height for some multifamily district) can, and this repo's gate.ts enforces the 999 sentinel by rule G7 whenever not_specified is set on max_height_ft, so the invariant is checked in code, not left to a convention. front_ft/rear_ft/side_ft/max_lot_coverage_pct/max_impervious_pct for SF-R/SF-1/SF-2 and MH/TF/TH/SR/MF-1/MF-2 (the non-SF-3 rows) are unchanged from whichever source table alone: SF-R/SF-1/SF-2 core dimensional cells were the two source tables' one point of full agreement; MH/TF/TH/SR/MF-1/MF-2 were carried from legacy-design-tools' table (this file did not previously ship them).
